create.model_decision_tip: Score actual output results via a large model, with evaluation criteria and scoring defined by prompts
create.code_decision_tip: Score actual output results by executing code functions, suitable for deterministic evaluation scenarios
create.word_placeholder: Please enter model judgment prompt, write variables using {{}} format

create.max_reply_tip: Used to limit the maximum number of Tokens for a single model generation. Tokens are the basic unit for model text processing, roughly 10 Tokens equals about 15 Chinese characters (length varies slightly due to punctuation, vocabulary structure, etc.). Setting a reasonable limit helps control output length and avoid overly long or redundant content.
create.generate_random_tip: This parameter controls the 'freedom' of the model during text generation. Higher values produce more diverse and creative output, potentially with novel or unexpected expressions; but also increase the chance of deviating from user intent or generating incoherent content. Lower values produce more deterministic, conservative output that aligns closely with common patterns in training data. To avoid conflicting effects, it's recommended not to adjust both this and 'Top P' significantly simultaneously.
create.top_n_tip: During each generation step, the model samples from the smallest vocabulary subset that reaches the cumulative probability threshold (e.g., Top P = 0.9). This means it considers only the most likely words at that moment, dynamically adjusting the candidate range rather than fixedly selecting the top N words. This method maintains language diversity while improving output reasonableness and coherence. As its mechanism overlaps with 'Generate Randomness', it's generally recommended to adjust only one of them for more predictable generation results.
create.user_word_tip: This prompt has the highest priority; the model will prioritize processing and evaluating its content.
create.debug_fail_reason: Model call failed, or try again after increasing 'Max Reply Length'
create.decision_score: Judgment score: Must output a numeric score. This value represents the alignment between the model output and the above scoring criteria (1.0 represents fully qualified, 0.0 represents fully unqualified).
create.decision_reason: Judgment reason: Briefly summarize the scoring rationale in one sentence, indicating which aspects met the standard and where deficiencies or errors exist.

evaluation_set.title: You don't have an evaluation dataset yet. Let's create one!
evaluation_set.desc: An evaluation dataset is a test dataset for evaluation. It typically contains input and reference output. You need to prepare an evaluation dataset before creating an evaluation task.

one.desc: Configure the required columns for the evaluation dataset according to evaluation needs. Standardize column names and types during configuration.

evaluation_task.title: You don't have an evaluation task yet. Let's create one now!
evaluation_task.desc: Evaluation involves conducting automated multi-dimensional assessments of an intelligent agent's output, such as correctness, relevance, and instruction adherence.

one.title: Create Evaluation Dataset
one.desc: , containing inputs and reference outputs. You need to prepare an evaluation dataset before starting an evaluation task.

two.title: Create Evaluator
two.desc: . Evaluators are divided into model judgment and code judgment. Evaluators act as referees to quantify evaluation results.

three.title: Create Evaluation Task
three.desc: . Selecting the evaluation target, evaluation dataset, and evaluator, launch the evaluation task to obtain results.

evaluator.title: You don't have an evaluator yet. Let's create one!
evaluator.desc: An evaluator defines evaluation criteria for users to judge the difference between reference output and actual output. The evaluator acts as a judge, quantifying the output results of the evaluation object to assess Agent task performance.

one.title: Configure Evaluation Rules
one.desc: Define the evaluation rules for the evaluator based on evaluation needs.

two.title: Debug
two.desc: Quickly verify if the evaluation logic is reasonable and results meet expectations by entering a set of test data.

three.title: Save Evaluator
three.desc: Submit and release an evaluator version. Once released, it can be used for subsequent evaluation tasks.
